answers.plain:
# 3-Day Budget Tokyo Itinerary (First-Timer)

**Rough budget:** ¥9,000–13,000/day (~$60–90) excluding flights and lodging.

## Before you go
- **Get a Suica/Pasmo** (add to your phone wallet if you have an iPhone) for trains and convenience stores.
- **Lodging:** Stay near a Yamanote Line station (Ueno, Asakusa, Shinjuku, Ikebukuro). Hostels or capsule hotels run ~¥3,000–6,000/night.
- **Cash:** Many small shops and shrines are cash-only. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards.
- **Transit pass:** A 72-hour Tokyo Subway Ticket (~¥1,500) pays off if you ride a lot. Otherwise, pay per ride with Suica.
- **Connectivity:** An eSIM is cheaper than pocket Wi-Fi.

## Day 1: Traditional Tokyo (Asakusa, Ueno)
- **Morning:** Sensō-ji Temple and Nakamise Street (free). Try fresh melon pan or ningyo-yaki as a snack.
- **Lunch:** Ramen or a teishoku set meal near Asakusa (¥800–1,200).
- **Afternoon:** Walk to Ueno Park (free). Optional: Tokyo National Museum (~¥1,000). Browse Ameyoko Market for snacks and cheap souvenirs.
- **Evening:** Take a free sunset view from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku (observation decks are free). Then dinner at Omoide Yokocho or a conveyor-belt sushi spot (¥1,500–2,500).

## Day 2: Pop culture and Shibuya/Harajuku
- **Morning:** Meiji Jingu shrine (free) through its forested approach.
- **Late morning:** Takeshita Street and Harajuku for crepes and people-watching. Walk down Omotesandō for architecture.
- **Lunch:** Gyudon (Sukiya, Matsuya, Yoshinoya) or a convenience store meal (¥500–800).
- **Afternoon:** Shibuya Crossing, Hachikō statue, and Shibuya Sky is pricey, so instead use the free view from the Shibuya Hikarie 11th-floor deck or Mag's Park rooftop (small fee).
- **Evening:** Explore Shimokitazawa for thrift shops and cheap izakaya, or go to Don Quijote for budget shopping.

## Day 3: Choose your flavor
- **Morning:** Tsukiji Outer Market for street food breakfast (tamagoyaki, seafood skewers; ¥1,500–2,500).
- **Late morning:** Hamarikyu Gardens (~¥300) or a walk along the Sumida River.
- **Afternoon, pick one:**
  - *Anime/tech:* Akihabara arcades and shops (free to browse).
  - *Quirky and local:* Nakano Broadway.
  - *Nature:* Yanaka district for old-Tokyo streets and cats.
- **Evening:** Farewell dinner at an izakaya, or a standing sushi bar. Optionally, see Tokyo Tower or Rainbow Bridge lit up at night from outside, which is free.

## Money-saving tips
- Eat at chain restaurants, standing noodle shops, and convenience stores. Quality is excellent.
- Lunch sets are much cheaper than dinner at the same restaurants.
- Tipping isn't done. Tap water is safe, so bring a refillable bottle.
- Many top sights (shrines, parks, crossings, observation decks) are free.
- Cluster each day geographically to minimize train fares.

## Estimated daily costs
| Item | Per day |
|---|---|
| Food | ¥3,000–4,500 |
| Transit | ¥600–1,000 |
| Activities | ¥0–1,500 |
| Lodging | ¥3,000–6,000 |

If you tell me your travel dates, budget ceiling, and interests (food, anime, nature, nightlife), I can tailor this further and adjust for seasonal things like autumn leaves or cherry blossoms.

# 3-Day Tokyo Budget Plan (First-Timer)

I assumed a solo traveler or couple, a mid-week arrival, and a target of about **¥8,000-10,000/day** for food, transit, and activities, plus lodging. Prices are approximate from my general knowledge and I haven't checked them live, so verify the key ones before booking. Tell me your dates, origin airport, and party size and I can tighten this.

## Strategy

- **Base in Ueno or Asakusa.** Hostels, capsules, and business hotels run about ¥3,500-7,000/night. Both have direct airport links (Keisei line to Narita) and sit on the Ginza and Hibiya subway lines. Shinjuku is the alternative if nightlife matters more, but it costs more.
- **Cluster by area.** Each day covers one region so you don't burn money and time crossing the city.
- **Spend on a few high-value things, not everything.** Tokyo's best experiences are cheap or free: shrines, markets, neighborhoods, and food.

## Transit

- **Get a Suica or Pasmo** in Apple/Google Wallet (iPhone, and many Android phones, are supported) or as a physical card. It works on trains, buses, vending machines, and convenience stores.
- **Consider the Tokyo Subway Ticket (24/48/72h, roughly ¥800-1,500).** It covers Tokyo Metro and Toei lines only, not JR (so not the Yamanote Line). Do the math: if you'll ride the subway 5+ times a day, it pays off. Otherwise Suica is simpler.
- **Airport:** Narita to Ueno via Keisei Access Express or Skyliner is cheaper than the Narita Express. Haneda is closer and cheap via Keikyu or monorail.
- Use Google Maps for routing. It handles platform numbers and transfers well.

## Day 1: Old Tokyo (Asakusa → Ueno → Akihabara)

| Time | Plan | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | **Senso-ji** and Nakamise street (go early to beat crowds). Try fresh melonpan or ningyo-yaki snacks | Free |
| Midday | Walk the Sumida River to a Skytree photo spot (skip the paid deck) | Free |
| Lunch | Asakusa side-street tempura or udon set, or a standing soba shop | ¥800-1,200 |
| Afternoon | **Ueno Park**, then **Ameyoko Market** for street food and snacks | Free + snacks |
| Evening | **Akihabara**: arcades, Super Potato retro games, Yodobashi | ¥500-1,000 for arcades |
| Dinner | Gyudon chain (Sukiya, Matsuya) or a ramen ticket-machine shop | ¥700-1,200 |

Day 1 is easy on purpose, since jet lag is real.

## Day 2: Modern Tokyo (Meiji → Harajuku → Shibuya → Shinjuku)

| Time | Plan | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | **Meiji Shrine**, a quiet forest walk | Free |
| Late morning | **Takeshita Street** (Harajuku) and **Omotesando** architecture. Check **Yoyogi Park** on weekends | Free |
| Lunch | Conveyor-belt sushi (Genki Sushi, Kappa Sushi) or a Harajuku crepe and konbini lunch | ¥1,000-1,500 |
| Afternoon | **Shibuya Crossing** and Hachiko. Optional **Shibuya Sky** at sunset, around ¥2,200 and worth it once if you book a timed slot online | Free / ~¥2,200 |
| Evening | **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building** observation deck in Shinjuku, a free alternative to Shibuya Sky | Free |
| Night | **Omoide Yokocho** for yakitori, then peek into **Golden Gai** (many bars charge a cover of ¥500-1,500, so check the sign first) | ¥1,500-3,000 |

If you do Shibuya Sky, skip the Government Building deck or vice versa, since the views overlap.

## Day 3: Food and Views (Tsukiji → Imperial Palace → Ginza → flexible evening)

| Time | Plan | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | **Tsukiji Outer Market**: tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, tuna bowls. Go hungry and early (before ~10am) | ¥1,500-2,500 |
| Late morning | **Imperial Palace East Gardens**, free and close by | Free |
| Afternoon | **Tokyo Station** (Marunouchi brick building, Ramen Street, Character Street) then window-shop in **Ginza** | Free |
| Evening (pick one) | **teamLab Planets or Borderless** (~¥3,800-4,500, book ahead, the one big-ticket splurge), **Nakameguro** canal walk, or **Shimokitazawa** for vintage shops and cafes | Varies |
| Last bites | Department store basement food halls (**depachika**) discount their prepared food after ~7pm | ¥500-1,000 |

## Cost Estimate (3 days, excluding flights)

| Category | Low | Comfortable |
|---|---|---|
| Lodging (2-3 nights) | ¥10,000 | ¥20,000 |
| Food | ¥9,000 | ¥15,000 |
| Local transit | ¥3,000 | ¥5,000 |
| Attractions | ¥0 | ¥6,000 |
| Airport transfers | ¥2,500 | ¥4,000 |
| **Total** | **~¥25,000** | **~¥50,000** |

## Money-Saving Tips

- Konbini (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) breakfasts are good: onigiri, egg sandwiches, and coffee for about ¥400.
- Tap water is safe. Carry a bottle and refill it.
- Tipping isn't done. Don't leave cash.
- Carry some cash (¥10,000-20,000). Many small shops and shrines are cash-only, although card use is growing. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards.
- Tax-free shopping (10%) at Don Quijote and large stores needs your passport and a minimum purchase, so bring it.
- Many places have no trash cans. Carry a small bag for rubbish.
- Eating or drinking while walking is considered rude in many places. Finish snacks near the stall.

## Booking Checklist

1. **Lodging**: book early, since prices spike on weekends and holidays.
2. **eSIM or pocket Wi-Fi**: eSIMs are the cheapest and easiest.
3. **Shibuya Sky or teamLab**: only if you want them, with timed slots.
4. **Visit Japan Web**: register before arrival for faster immigration and customs.

## Backups

- **Rain:** swap in the Edo-Tokyo Museum area (if open, check status), Ueno's museums (the Tokyo National Museum is about ¥1,000), or covered arcades like Asakusa's Nakamise and Ameyoko.
- **Extra energy:** replace the Day 3 evening with a half-day to **Kamakura** (about 1 hour by train), with its Great Buddha and coastal temples.

If you share your dates, budget ceiling, and interests (food, anime, nature, nightlife), I can adjust the days and give a more precise cost.

# 3-Day Tokyo Itinerary (Budget, First-Timer)

**Verification status:** I had no web access in this session, so I could not check any price, hour, or closure day against an official page. Everything below comes from memory and should be treated as an **estimate (Est.)** until you confirm it. I name the official source for each item so you can check it quickly. Fares and hours change, and JR East announced a fare revision for 2026 that I can't confirm.

## Assumptions
- **Arrival:** Haneda or Narita, on a separate "Day 0" (transfer cost listed below, not in the daily totals).
- **Hostel:** Near **Ueno Station** (Yamanote, Ginza, and Hibiya lines, plus the Keisei line to Narita). Ueno puts Asakusa, the Yamanote loop, and Tsukiji all within one short ride.
- **Budget:** ¥10,000-12,000/day excluding lodging, so ¥30,000-36,000 for the three days.
- **Dates:** Unknown, so I built in the closure rules you'll need (see "Date rules").

**Airport to Ueno (Est.):**
- **Narita:** Keisei Access Express or Rapid, about ¥1,300-1,500. Avoid the Skyliner (about ¥2,500+) on this budget.
- **Haneda:** Keikyu to Shinagawa, then JR Yamanote to Ueno, about ¥550-650.

## Day 1: Old Tokyo (Ueno, Yanaka, Asakusa)
**Lines:** Walking, then Tokyo Metro Ginza Line (Ueno to Asakusa, 2 stops).

| Time | Stop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | **Ueno Park** and **Ameyoko** market street (browse) | Free |
| Late morning | **Wander block: Yanaka** (Yanaka Ginza shopping street, temples, old cemetery), a 20-minute walk from Ueno. Most tourists skip it. | Free |
| Afternoon | Ginza Line to Asakusa, then **Senso-ji** and Nakamise-dori | Free (omikuji ¥100) |
| Evening | Stroll along the Sumida River, then dinner | |

- **Senso-ji:** grounds open 24h. Main hall about 6:00 (6:30 Oct-Mar) to 17:00. Nakamise shops usually run about 9:00-17:00 or 18:00 (Est.). Check senso-ji.jp.
- **Meals:**
  - Breakfast: 7-Eleven/Lawson onigiri and coffee (~¥400).
  - Lunch: menchi-katsu snacks in Yanaka plus onigiri (~¥1,000, Est.).
  - Dinner: **Tenya** tempura-bowl chain (~¥800-1,000, Est.), or **Matsuya** or **Sukiya** beef bowls.
- **Transit:** Ueno to Asakusa ¥180 (Metro adult fare table), plus return ¥180, so **¥360**.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Transit | ¥360 |
| Meals | ¥2,400 |
| Snacks/drinks, omikuji | ¥500 |
| **Day 1 total** | **~¥3,260** |

## Day 2: West Side (Harajuku, Shibuya, Shinjuku)
**Lines:** Ginza Line (Ueno to Omotesando), then walking, then JR Yamanote (Shibuya to Shinjuku to Ueno).

| Time | Stop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Ginza Line to **Omotesando**, walk the avenue to Harajuku, then **Meiji Jingu** (forest path, free) | Free |
| Midday | **Takeshita-dori**, then **Yoyogi Park** | Free |
| Afternoon | **Wander block: Cat Street and the Ura-Harajuku back lanes**, walking down to Shibuya (about 20 min) | Free |
| Dusk | **Shibuya Crossing** (view from the Shibuya Station area or the Magnet/Starbucks windows, all free) | Free |
| Night | JR to Shinjuku, then the **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building** free observatory | Free |

- **Meiji Jingu:** open sunrise to sunset, so the closing time shifts through the year. The inner garden costs extra (~¥500, skip it). Check meijijingu.or.jp.
- **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building:**
  - North observatory is about 9:30-22:00 (Est.), closed 2nd and 4th Mondays.
  - South observatory closes earlier (~17:30, Est.) and is closed 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.
  - Check the official observatory page (yokoso.metro.tokyo.lg.jp) before going.
- **Meals:**
  - Breakfast: konbini (~¥400).
  - Lunch: gyoza set in Harajuku (~¥1,000, Est.).
  - Dinner: **Ichiran** ramen in Shinjuku (~¥1,100-1,300, Est.), or **Uobei** conveyor sushi in Shibuya (~¥1,000 for a full meal).
- **Transit (Est.):** Ueno to Omotesando ~¥210, Shibuya to Shinjuku ~¥170, Shinjuku to Ueno ~¥240. That is **~¥620**.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Transit | ~¥620 |
| Meals | ~¥2,500 |
| Snacks (crepe) | ¥500 |
| **Day 2 total** | **~¥3,620** |

## Day 3: Central and East (Tsukiji, Imperial Palace, Jimbocho, Akihabara)
**Lines:** Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line (Ueno to Tsukiji), then walking, then JR (Akihabara to Ueno).

| Time | Stop | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Hibiya Line to **Tsukiji**, then **Outer Market** breakfast | ~¥800 |
| Late morning | Walk through **Ginza** to the **Imperial Palace East Gardens** (about 2 km) | Free |
| Afternoon | **Wander block: Jimbocho** second-hand bookshop district (about 2 km north of the gardens) | Free |
| Late afternoon | **Akihabara** (arcades, window-shopping), then JR back to Ueno | Free |

- **Tsukiji Outer Market:** most stalls run from early morning to about 14:00 (Est.) and are closed Sundays, holidays, and some Wednesdays. Verify against the market's calendar.
- **Imperial Palace East Gardens:** free, about 9:00 to 16:30-17:00 depending on season (Est.), **closed Mondays and Fridays**. Check the Imperial Household Agency page (kunaicho.go.jp).
- **Meals:**
  - Breakfast: tamagoyaki and onigiri at Tsukiji (~¥800).
  - Lunch: katsu curry in Jimbocho, e.g. **Kitchen Nankai** (~¥1,000, Est.; unverified, check that it's open).
  - Dinner: **Coco Ichibanya** curry chain (~¥1,000).
- **Transit (Est.):** Ueno to Tsukiji ~¥180-210, Akihabara to Ueno ¥150, so **~¥360**.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Transit | ~¥360 |
| Meals | ~¥2,800 |
| Snacks | ¥300 |
| **Day 3 total** | **~¥3,460** |

## Date rules
- Day 3 only works on **Tue, Thu, or Sat**. Mondays and Fridays shut the East Gardens, and Sundays, holidays, and some Wednesdays shut much of Tsukiji.
- Avoid Day 2 on the 2nd/4th Monday (north observatory closed) or the 1st/3rd Tuesday (south observatory closed).

## Ticket comparison for this specific route
Using Tokyo Metro/Toei and JR East adult fares from memory (Est.):

| Option | Cost for this itinerary |
|---|---|
| **Pay-per-ride** (IC or paper) | **~¥1,340** in fares |
| Tokyo Subway Ticket 72h (~¥1,500 Est.) | Costs more than the fares themselves, and doesn't cover JR rides (Day 2's Shibuya to Shinjuku to Ueno and Day 3's Akihabara to Ueno) |
| 24h/48h Subway Ticket | Doesn't cover three days of this route, and doesn't pay back on 1-2 days |

**Verdict:** pay-per-ride beats the Subway Ticket here. For convenience, load a **mobile Suica or PASMO into Apple Wallet** (no issuance fee, if you have an iPhone). A physical PASMO Passport adds a non-refundable ¥500 fee (Est.), so paper tickets are the cheapest by a few hundred yen if you want to avoid cards entirely. Confirm all fares on the Tokyo Metro, Toei, and JR East fare-search pages.

## Budget Totals
| Day | Cost |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | ~¥3,260 |
| Day 2 | ~¥3,620 |
| Day 3 | ~¥3,460 |
| **Total** | **~¥10,340** |
| Assumed budget (3 days) | ¥30,000-36,000 |
| **Surplus** | **~¥19,700-25,700** |

That surplus covers the airport transfer, a paid viewpoint like Shibuya Sky (price unverified), the Tokyo National Museum (~¥1,000, closed Mondays, Est.), or a nicer dinner.

## What would sharpen this plan most
**Your actual dates and hotel location.** Dates decide which days the East Gardens, Tsukiji, and the observatories are open. The hotel decides the real fares and whether a different line grouping would be shorter.
